title: SAT Math: Content, Calculator & Grid-Ins
summary: The Digital SAT Math section — what it covers, the built-in calculator on every question, and the grid-in answers to watch.

nodes.label: Calculator always
nodes.note: Built-in Desmos on every Math question

chunks.heading: Four content areas
chunks.body: Math covers **Algebra** (linear equations, systems, inequalities), **Advanced Math** (quadratics, functions, exponents), **Problem-Solving and Data Analysis** (ratios, percentages, statistics, reading graphs), and **Geometry and Trigonometry** (area, volume, angles, right triangles). Algebra and Advanced Math make up the bulk.
chunks.realExample: A typical question gives a word problem you must translate into an equation — the maths is high-school level; the skill is turning the words into algebra correctly.
chunks.memoryHook: Algebra + Advanced Math dominate. Most questions = translate words into an equation.

chunks.heading: The calculator is on every question
chunks.body: A **built-in Desmos graphing calculator is available on all 44 Math questions** (you can also bring an approved one). Desmos can **graph equations to solve them visually** — often faster than algebra. But don't over-rely on it: many questions are quicker by reasoning.
chunks.realExample: For 'where do these two lines intersect?', typing both into Desmos and reading the intersection point is faster and less error-prone than solving the system by hand.
chunks.memoryHook: Desmos on every question — learn to graph-and-read. But reason first when it's faster.

chunks.heading: Watch the grid-in (student-produced) answers
chunks.body: Most questions are multiple choice, but **some ask you to type the answer** (no options). These 'grid-ins' have **no choices to check your work against**, so double-check the **format** — fractions or decimals are fine, but follow any instruction and don't round unless told to.
chunks.realExample: If the answer is 7/3, you can enter '7/3' or a decimal like '2.33' — but entering '2.3' (over-rounded) can be marked wrong. Enter enough digits.
chunks.memoryHook: Grid-ins have no options — mind the format and don't over-round.

chunks.heading: Adaptive + no penalty — pace and attempt everything
chunks.body: Math is **two-stage adaptive**, so **module 1 sets your ceiling** — give the first module your best. With **no penalty for wrong answers**, always put something for every question, and use the **flag tool** to bank easy points first, then return to hard ones.
chunks.realExample: About 95 seconds per question. Stuck at two minutes? Flag it, guess, move on — a skipped question you never return to is a guaranteed zero.
chunks.memoryHook: Module 1 = ceiling. No penalty = never blank. Easy points first, flag the rest.

recall.q: What four content areas does SAT Math cover?
recall.a: Algebra, Advanced Math, Problem-Solving and Data Analysis, and Geometry and Trigonometry.

recall.q: Is a calculator allowed on SAT Math?
recall.a: Yes — a built-in Desmos graphing calculator is available on all Math questions (you may also bring an approved one).
You type the answer with no options, so you must mind the format and avoid over-rounding.

recall.q: Why does the first Math module matter most?
recall.a: Math is two-stage adaptive, so module 1 determines the difficulty of module 2 and your scoring ceiling.

recall.q: How should you handle a hard Math question under time pressure?
recall.a: Flag it, put a best-guess answer (no penalty for wrong), and move on — banking easy points first.
